transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah. I guess my lieutenant thought I needed to come in. At the station I was, uh, reorganizing some of the airway bags in the bay—just trying to get them in the right pattern, I guess—and I was saying some dispatch numbers out loud.

I know that probably sounds odd. I wasn’t trying to make trouble or anything. He told me to stop, and I… I had a hard time stepping away because it felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad somehow. So they sent me here. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you feel that breaking the sequence might make the bay 'go bad,' do you recognize at the time that this fear might not be realistic, or does it feel completely true to you?

I mean… I can see how it might sound a little much when I say it here. I’m not trying to be difficult or make myself look, you know, unstable.

But at the time it feels pretty real. Like with the bay, it’s not just the bags. I get this feeling that people are watching what I’m doing through the station cameras… the injury review people, and some supervisors. And sometimes I’m pretty sure my triage notes are getting changed so it looks like I’m unsafe, even when they say it’s just routine paperwork.

I know you might tell me that’s not likely, and I’m trying to be open to that. But when it’s happening, it doesn’t feel like just a worry. It feels like I’m seeing what’s going on. Is that… is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or new medications—prescribed or otherwise—around the time these experiences started?

Um… I don’t think so. Not that I can point to, anyway.

I mean, I’ll have a drink once in a while, but I’m not— I don’t think it’s anything unusual. And I haven’t been taking anything new that I can think of. No drugs or anything like that.

If there’s something specific you’re asking about, I can try to answer better. I just don’t want to leave something out if it matters.
How long has it been since you first started noticing these feelings—like the cameras watching you or your notes being changed—days, weeks, or longer?

Um… I’d say longer than days. I don’t want to overstate it, but the camera stuff and feeling like the paperwork is being changed… probably around two months now.

The station thing that got everyone worried, that’s been in that same stretch too, I think. Maybe it built up, but… yeah, about the last couple months. Is that helpful?
Aside from feeling watched or that your notes are being altered, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear?

Um… I don’t think so. Not voices, no.

I mean, sometimes I’ll hear little noises and look around, but I think that’s just normal stuff, especially after work or when I’m tired. I haven’t had, like, someone talking to me when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean.

I’m trying to answer it the right way—if you mean something more subtle than that, I can think about it.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, high fevers, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions—like thyroid problems or neurological issues—around the time these experiences started?

Um… no, not that I know of. I haven’t had a head injury or seizures or anything like that.

No high fevers that I can remember, and I haven’t been told I have thyroid problems or anything neurological. I mean, not that I’m aware of. If there’s something I should be checking, I can, but I don’t think there’s anything like that around when this started.
Over these past couple of months, have you noticed any changes in your energy, motivation, or interest in things you used to enjoy, or found yourself pulling away from friends, family, or coworkers?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

Most days when I’m not working, I kind of just end up sitting in my apartment. I’ve got stuff there I should deal with, like trash in the corner, food still in the fridge that I bought thinking I’d cook, and then I just… don’t. I used to cook more, and I used to call the guys to play basketball, but lately I don’t really reach out.

It’s not that I hate anyone or anything. I just can’t seem to get myself to care enough or start doing things. Is that the kind of change you mean?

Before these two months when the camera and paperwork concerns started, did you notice any earlier changes—even subtle ones, like feeling a bit 'off,' more withdrawn, or less like yourself—going back further, say four to six months ago?

I guess… yeah, maybe going back farther than two months.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it kind of started after I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer, about eight months ago. After that I just felt a little off, I think. At the time I figured it was just because I was banged up and tired, so I didn’t really make a big deal of it.

Does that answer what you mean?
During these past several months, have you been feeling consistently sad, down, or hopeless, most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not like sad all day every day.

I mean, I’ve had some rough days and I get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’m consistently hopeless or depressed most of the day. At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing. Is that an okay way to answer it?

During these past several months, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or 'on top of the world,' needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like you could do things others couldn't?

No… I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.

I mean, I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep great, but not because I felt amazing or like I didn’t need it. And I wouldn’t say I’ve been “on top of the world” or had some burst of energy. If anything, I’ve mostly just been trying to get through the day.

Is that what you mean?

Since that shoulder injury about eight months ago, have you been feeling 'off,' withdrawn, or not like yourself continuously the whole time, or were there periods in between where you felt completely back to normal before the camera and paperwork concerns started two months ago?

I don’t think I ever felt totally back to normal, honestly… but it wasn’t like it was intense the whole time.

It’s hard to explain. After I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer, about eight months ago, that’s when I started feeling kind of off. I kept telling myself it was just the injury or stress, and there were probably better stretches, but I don’t know that I’d say I was completely myself again before the camera and paperwork stuff started.

Is that the kind of timeline you’re asking for?

Total symptom duration (~8 months) now supports schizophrenia over schizophreniform disorder, though the latter remains possible if strict active-phase duration is used instead.

doctor.intent: Assess for any manic or hypomanic symptoms (elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity) that might have co-occurred with the psychotic symptoms, to rule out a mood component consistent with schizoaffective disorder
doctor.question: During these past several months, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or 'on top of the world,' needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like you could do things others couldn't?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about manic or hypomanic symptoms such as elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, or grandiosity, which are not covered by the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.

I mean, I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep great, but not because I felt amazing or like I didn’t need it. And I wouldn’t say I’ve been “on top of the world” or had some burst of energy. If anything, I’ve mostly just been trying to get through the day.

Is that what you mean?

inference.note: Absence of any depressive or manic episodes over the illness course argues against schizoaffective disorder (F25.9), and the presence of disorganized ritualistic behavior plus prominent negative symptoms (avolition, social withdrawal) alongside multi-domain delusions makes isolated delusional disorder (F22) less likely, leaving schizophrenia spectrum diagnoses as most probable.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the overall disturbance (including prodromal withdrawal/functioning changes) has been continuous for at least 6 months, which distinguishes schizophrenia from schizophreniform disorder
doctor.question: Since that shoulder injury about eight months ago, have you been feeling 'off,' withdrawn, or not like yourself continuously the whole time, or were there periods in between where you felt completely back to normal before the camera and paperwork concerns started two months ago?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This all started after I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer about eight months ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the time course since the shoulder injury about eight months ago and whether symptoms were continuous or remitted before the last two months.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I ever felt totally back to normal, honestly… but it wasn’t like it was intense the whole time.

It’s hard to explain. After I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer, about eight months ago, that’s when I started feeling kind of off. I kept telling myself it was just the injury or stress, and there were probably better stretches, but I don’t know that I’d say I was completely myself again before the camera and paperwork stuff started.

Is that the kind of timeline you’re asking for?
